tasks.title: perception: replay a video on CPU into ObservationFrame JSONL
tasks.goal: A laptop with no Pi can turn a kitchen video into tracked ObservationFrame JSONL, so every downstream team has realistic input from day one. The Detector interface introduced here is what the Hailo backend plugs into later.
acceptance: `uv run --package perception python -m perception.replay --video <file> --out frames.jsonl` writes one ObservationFrame per processed frame
A Detector interface exists, with a CPU backend using pretrained YOLOv8 detection (knife, spoon, fork, bowl) plus YOLOv8 pose wrists. Tracking runs through ByteTrack behind a Tracker interface
Hands are emitted as kind=hand, class_name=wrist, with person_id and wrist [x, y, conf]. Bowls are emitted as kind=plate. Tools as kind=tool
Every line validates: `uv run --package perception pytest components/perception/tests/test_replay_contract.py`
Frame t_ms comes from the injected Clock (video timestamps) and is strictly increasing: covered by a `safety` test
Running the replay twice on the same input produces identical JSONL: `pytest -k deterministic`
The sample clip is referenced in `components/perception/data-manifest.json` (not committed). A tiny fixture of 50 KB or less is committed under tests/fixtures/
README documents the command and the AGPL-3.0 note for ultralytics. A `status:needs-human` question to the owner about licensing is filed
out_of_scope: Bins and zones (slot identity comes in perception-03 and perception-04)

tasks.title: perception: spike Hailo-8 YOLOv8 det+pose feasibility and FPS
tasks.goal: Find out, with measurements, whether compiled HEFs exist for YOLOv8 detection and YOLOv8 pose on the Hailo-8, and what FPS we get running both on one Hailo-8 with the Pi camera.
acceptance: The issue has a written answer: HEF names and sources, and the exact Pi OS, HailoRT and Python versions
A benchmark script `components/perception/scripts/hailo_bench.py`, plus step-by-step owner instructions posted on the issue
Owner-posted FPS for detection alone, pose alone, and both together, at at least two input resolutions
A recommendation (both every frame / pose every Nth frame / smaller models / CPU fallback), with a team ADR drafted if the plan deviates from ARCHITECTURE

tasks.title: perception: zone calibration format, tool and zone RFC
tasks.goal: Bin slots, the plating spot, the wash station and the pass are defined once as normalized polygons, and every detection gets a zone. The zone table currently has no contract schema, so this task also proposes one.
acceptance: Zone file format (zone_id, kind in bin_slot | plating_spot | wash | pass | other, polygon of normalized points), with a validator test
`uv run --package perception python -m perception.zones.calibrate --image <still.jpg> --out zones.json` lets a person click polygons and save them
Point-in-polygon zone assignment for detections, with unit tests covering edges and overlapping zones (deterministic tie-break)
A sample zones.json is committed under tests/fixtures/ for interactions and experience
A `type:rfc` issue proposes a `zone` schema in contracts/ and `StateClient.set_zones`, since both are missing from contracts today

tasks.title: perception: entity identity rules with new-ID-on-reacquire
tasks.goal: Map tracker IDs to stable entity IDs (bin-<slot>, tool-<class>-<n>, hand-p<k>-left/right, plate-<n>) so a lost and re-acquired track is always a new entity with unknown history (invariant 8).
acceptance: An identity module assigns entity_id and first_seen_t_ms from track IDs, classes, slots and pose person IDs
`safety` test: a track lost beyond the track buffer and re-acquired gets a new entity_id, with first_seen_t_ms equal to when it reappeared
`safety` property test (hypothesis): entity IDs are never reused within a shift, over random track lifetimes
`safety` test: a person re-acquired by pose gets new hand IDs

Every entity gets origin: shift_start (seen before shift start), clean_stack (first seen leaving a clean_stack zone) or unknown (anything else, including re-acquired tracks). `safety` test: a re-acquired track is always unknown
Bins take their ID from their slot zone (bin-4 is whatever sits in slot-4). The README documents that swapping bins between slots mid-shift is unsupported
`uv run --package perception pytest components/perception -m safety` passes
out_of_scope: Any re-identification or merging of tracks (that would need an RFC and the safety reviewer)

tasks.title: perception: publish recorded frame JSONL fixture pack
tasks.goal: Ship the fake that consumers test against: small, real, recorded ObservationFrame JSONL clips covering the core interaction shapes.
acceptance: At least 3 fixtures under `components/perception/tests/fixtures/pack/`: knife scoop in a bin slot, hand touching a plate, and a tool leaving the frame and re-entering (new entity ID)
Each fixture is 100 KB or less, validates against observation_frame, and has a README line saying what happens and when
A replay source can stream a fixture pack file in-process: `pytest -k fixture_pack`
Announced on the interactions Team board with paths
out_of_scope: Labels or expected events (interactions owns those)

tasks.title: perception: entity store and 5 Hz sync via StateClient
tasks.goal: Keep every frame's entities in memory on the Pi and push entity rows to SpacetimeDB at about 5 Hz through StateClient.upsert_entities, without ever blocking the frame loop.
acceptance: An in-memory store holds the latest Entity per entity_id, plus a bounded frame history (configurable)
Sync calls upsert_entities at 5 Hz ±10%, measured with FakeClock in a test, in batches of 30 entities or fewer
StateUnavailable is retried with backoff. The frame loop never blocks on sync (test with a slow fake). Sync lag is exposed for /v1/health
Stale entities keep last_seen_t_ms and are never deleted
Fake-swap test runs replay → store → sync against InMemoryStateClient: `pytest -k sync`
out_of_scope: Allergen profile fields (intake and provenance tables)

tasks.title: perception: POST /v1/plates/start binds exactly one plate
tasks.goal: When the cook taps start ticket, bind the single plate in the plating-spot zone to the ticket and write plate_binding. Never guess.
acceptance: Exactly one plate in plating_spot calls StateClient.bind_plate(plate_id, ticket_id, t_ms) and returns {plate_id}
No plate returns 409 no_plate_at_spot. Two or more plates return 409 multiple_plates_at_spot. Both are `safety` tests
A plate already bound to a different ticket is refused, never silently rebound. The error code is proposed via RFC, since it's not in apis.md yet
Error bodies follow {"error": {"code", "message"}}
`uv run --package perception pytest components/perception -k plates_start` passes against InMemoryStateClient

tasks.title: perception: GET /v1/health and GET /stream.mjpg
tasks.goal: Expose liveness for the pass gate (which faults when health goes stale) and the raw camera stream for overlays.
acceptance: /v1/health returns {fps, hailo, last_frame_t_ms}. last_frame_t_ms stops advancing when frames stop (`safety` test with a stalled source)
/stream.mjpg serves MJPEG from the active source. A smoke test reads at least 3 JPEG parts
Endpoints never block the frame loop (test with a slow client)
README shows curl commands for both

tasks.title: perception: frame recorder with byte-identical replay
tasks.goal: Record any source's ObservationFrames to JSONL with a session manifest, and replay them so downstream output is identical. This underpins M2's deterministic live-session replay.
acceptance: `python -m perception.record --source <video|camera> --out <dir>` writes frames.jsonl plus manifest.json (source, versions, zones file hash, shift start, model versions)
Record then replay round-trips byte-identically: `pytest -k roundtrip`
The replay source preserves recorded t_ms and can pace in real time or run as fast as possible
Large recordings go to data/ (gitignored), with a manifest entry format documented

tasks.title: perception: FakePerceptionAPI for experience
tasks.goal: Give experience a stand-in for the Pi so they can build the start-ticket button, the gate fault logic and overlays without hardware.
acceptance: `uv run --package perception python -m perception.fake_api --port 8080` serves the three Perception HTTP API endpoints
/v1/plates/start answers from a script file (success, no_plate_at_spot, multiple_plates_at_spot) in sequence
/v1/health can be made stale on command, to exercise gate fault
/stream.mjpg loops a generated test pattern (no committed video)
Contract tests check response shapes against apis.md: `pytest -k fake_api`

tasks.title: perception: sync entities to local SpacetimeDB via real StateClient
tasks.goal: Swap the fake for the real StateClient, and prove replayed entities land in a local SpacetimeDB at the target rate.
acceptance: Replay of the fixture pack, then store, then real StateClient: rows are visible in the entity table (query shown in the PR)
5 Hz sustained for 10 minutes of replay without a growing backlog (log excerpt in the PR)
Killing the DB mid-run raises StateUnavailable, health shows sync lag, and sync recovers when the DB returns
The command to reproduce is in the README

tasks.title: perception: Hailo detector backend behind Detector interface
tasks.goal: Implement the Hailo-8 backend chosen by the perception-02 spike behind the same Detector interface as the CPU backend, so M2 only has to flip a config switch.
acceptance: A Hailo backend implements Detector. CPU and Hailo outputs share one contract test run on a recorded image set (Hailo half skipped in CI via the `hardware` marker)
Backend choice is config-only (PERCEPTION_DETECTOR=cpu|hailo)
An owner test script on the issue: exact commands to run on the Pi, and the expected FPS and output
Issue moves to status:needs-human until the owner posts results
out_of_scope: Performance tuning beyond the spike's recommendation
